T3.title: Table 3. Directional 30-Minute WTI Return (Percent) by Class Under Each Label Set
rows: Human minus label set, escalation: difference (95% CI), p
T3.note: Same 95 events under every label set. p-values are two-sided Wilcoxon tests. Differences use a day-clustered bootstrap with 10,000 resamples; the two-sided p is taken from the bootstrap distribution. The v2 opus run gives the same results as the majority for both classes (33 and 30 events). On the investigator-adjudicated labels, the human estimates were 1.05% (n = 29) and 0.48% (n = 16), and the escalation difference for model 1 was +0.31 (0.02, 0.65), p = .04.

T4.title: Table 4. Misclassification Decomposition of the Model-Label Estimates
T4.note: Final human labels. Entries in the human-label columns are the number of model-labelled events with that human label and, in parentheses, their mean directional 30-minute return (percent) signed in the direction of the model’s class. In Panel A, the fourth column counts human de-escalation posts; in Panel B, human escalation posts. The gap column lists, in order, selection within the class, then contamination by the human class in the fourth column, by mixed posts, and by other posts. Components are rounded and need not sum exactly.
